A traveling PARTICLE follows a geodesic; a propagating FRONT refracts (Fermat / eikonal): the transverse gradient of the effective index tilts the front. For a source with potential phi(r), a front passing at impact parameter b deflects by delta(b) = int over the path of the transverse derivative = int_{-inf}^{inf} d/db[phi(sqrt(b^2+z^2))] dz. This is the standard eikonal lensing integral (the Eddington optical analogy for light-bending), cited as real-analysis provenance (as container 16 cites the trig). The point of this container is that delta(b)'s FORM -- impact-independent, 1/b, or other -- is fixed once phi's radial profile is, and phi's profile is fixed by the source-flux dimension (DF.2/DF.3). Danger-free: no mass in the form (mass only scales the magnitude, DF.6).
